No verdict changes (threshold slope 1).
exact 18138.4562; summary.md prints 18138.5 and the README rounds that to 18139; a single rounding gives 18138. Within the README's documented rounding chain (0.05 + 0.5).
measured 16-bit S/rho is 6.4452 (w=0), 6.6323 (w=0.1), 7.6607 (w=1). '6.5' is not a rounding of the w=0.1 value (6.6). The README table value 6.63 is used as the claim.

discrepancies.what: arm (b) full-IC S omits the S5 interpolation
discrepancies.detail: in `fullic --arm b` S5 is built once per process outside every run's counted phases (setup.build = [0] in all 32 arm-(b) full-IC records), while the tdec-b setup records count [14467005] build operations for it, and PROTOCOL's S covers 'table or S5' cold. Priced at w, this understates arm (b) S(0.1) and S(1) by 1.06% at bx=3 and 0.10% at bx=4 (resultant evaluations are uncounted by design). Arm (a) and rho are unaffected; no ranking changes. Not disclosed in the README.

README: 'dimension 0 for random targets, 24 or 12 for planted'. At 16 bits bx=8, planted target 16 has dimension 48 = brute-force root count 48 (a second decomposition). The control (dimension equals the brute-force count, planted point vanishes) holds; only the README wording is incomplete.

at HEAD 44578da212c808280f071d2fb0c45bc47ed905e2 benchmarks/README.md has no row for 20261018-blindspots-prime-m4-cells; the assess commit bde5b137c7 added only REPORT.pdf, graph.svg and graph.png (byte-identical to the research copies). The 'benchmarks row' claims checked are the commit subject's (slope 11.03; 6.5x-30x).

limitations: Derived fits use mixed conventions: the README's 0.179 growth, p^0.60 and p^0.42 reproduce with x = the cell label (16, 20, 24, 28) at w = 0 only. log2(S/rho) growth on the cell label is 0.1787 / 0.1758 / 0.1606 at w = 0 / 0.1 / 1; on log2 of the actual primes it is 0.1728 / 0.1700 / 0.1553. S exponent on actual primes 0.588, rho 0.415 at w = 0. The summarizer's arm-(a) T_dec fit uses actual primes. 'The gap grows with p' holds under every convention.

The matched rho is a plain r-adding walk over points. The x-keyed DP table catches +-matches only at distinguished points; it is not a negation-map walk. The strongest reference for these curves (j != 0, 1728) is negation (expected about 1/sqrt(2) of the walk steps, heuristic). A stronger rho could only lower rho's cost and widen the measured gap, so the order 'rho is cheaper' is unaffected; the ratios are understated.
DP parameter theta = floor(bits/4) uses the cell label (4, 5, 6, 7 bits), as PROTOCOL's 'log2 p' convention does; with log2 of the actual prime it would be one bit smaller at every cell.

The rho binary has no recorded sha256 (deleted by the card's remove-bin step). Binary identity rests on the receipt: one build of target/blindspots-14/card-01/b14 from the bound source at a clean commit, then every rho and arm-(a) run invokes that path. Arm (b) full IC (cards 09-12) used separate rustc builds of the same source and flags, not the same binary file as the rho.

One curve per size, 16 runs per cell; rho means have about 13% standard error at 16 runs. Full-IC targets are a correlated walk (Deviation 11). Toy scale (16-28 bits); arm (b)'s p-exponent assumes |F| = p^(1/4) and extrapolates beyond |F| = 6..16.
